subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should maintainers approve making the isolated `workspaceAccess: "none"` sandbox workspace writable across all sandbox backends while preserving host-workspace isolation and read-only protected mounts?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes sandbox write authorization and should not be queued without explicit security/product ownership of the final contract and proof shape.

options.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
options.body: Implement the cross-backend fix that makes only the sandbox-owned `/workspace` writable for `none` while keeping real workspace isolation and protected roots intact.

options.title: Keep Current Fail-Closed Behavior
options.body: Leave `none` read-only and update docs/tool exposure to say isolated sandbox workspaces cannot support write-heavy workflows in that mode.

options.title: Write Policy Note First
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers publish a short sandbox write-policy note covering isolated workspaces, custom binds, skill roots, and remote backends.

recommendation.title: Approve Isolated-Writable None
recommendation.body: Implement the cross-backend fix that makes only the sandbox-owned `/workspace` writable for `none` while keeping real workspace isolation and protected roots intact.

likelyOwner.reason: This account is the clearest individual routing owner from recent sandbox history and the explicit canonical-issue comment on the related workaround PR.
